drug_class: Rho kinase (ROCK) inhibitor / norepinephrine transport inhibitor eye drop
purpose: Netarsudil is an eye drop used to lower eye pressure in people with glaucoma or a condition called ocular hypertension (high pressure in the eye). Keeping eye pressure under control helps protect your vision and prevents damage to the optic nerve. Your doctor has prescribed it to help keep your eyes healthy.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes and drains a fluid called aqueous humor. In glaucoma, this fluid does not drain well enough, causing pressure to build up. Netarsudil works by relaxing and opening up the drainage channels in your eye so fluid can flow out more easily, lowering the pressure inside your eye.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is redness of the eye or eyelids, which many patients notice. You may also see small, visible red lines on the white of your eye (called conjunctival hyperemia). Other possible side effects include mild eye discomfort or stinging when you put the drop in, watery eyes, and a deposit or small line that may appear on your cornea (the clear front part of your eye) — your doctor will check for this during visits. Some people notice their eye color or eyelid skin may darken slightly over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you wear contact lenses — you should remove them before putting in the drop and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Do not use this drop if you are allergic to any of its ingredients. Let your doctor know about all other eye drops or medications you are taking. If you experience severe eye pain, sudden vision changes, or signs of an eye infection, contact your doctor right away. Safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established, so talk to your doctor if this applies to you.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye or eyes once every evening, at bedtime. Try to use it at the same time each night. If you miss a dose, just skip it and use your next dose the following evening — do not double up. Wash your hands before using the drops, tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid gently, and place one drop inside. Close your eye for about one to two minutes and press gently on the inner corner of your eye to help keep the drop in place.
